bottleneck: The brain's immune system — microglia, border-associated macrophages, meningeal immunity — constantly surveils and sculpts neural circuits, but the signaling language between immune cells and neurons is largely undeciphered. Immune molecules like complement and cytokines modulate synaptic plasticity, learning, and behavior, yet neuroimmunology cannot predict when immune activity helps cognition and when it harms it. Two extraordinarily complex systems interact through unknown protocols, and single-cell atlases have produced a census without a grammar. Every brain disease has an immune dimension that cannot be rationally targeted.
current_state: Single-cell atlases map brain immune cells in exquisite detail, but functional understanding of neuroimmune signaling lags far behind the census, and no neuroimmune therapy is approved.

title: Neuroimmune signaling language undeciphered
why_it_blocks: Immunity shapes every brain disease from Alzheimer's to depression, yet the conversation between immune cells and neurons is untranslated. Decoding it could unify neurology and immunology into a single therapeutic science.
